cohort: The study included women who gave birth at Sebelas Maret University Hospital, Surakarta, between January 2020 and January 2022 and used either IUDs or tubectomy for contraception.
finding: The study found that while the use of IUDs and tubectomy for contraception remained stable during the COVID-19 pandemic, there was a decrease in postpartum in-person visits and an increase in hospitalizations.
mod_finding: 66% of IUD insertions were conducted via vaginal delivery while 84% of tubectomies were performed via cesarean section.
